title: Failure injection, recovery and runbooks
objectives: Model a bounded pure recovery phase machine with expected epoch and explicit reconciliation evidence before approval/resumption.

Design scoped failure-injection/runbook evidence distinguishing detection, mitigation, unknown committed effects, recovery verification and post-incident learning without claiming actual recovery execution.
Apply failure injection, recovery and runbooks invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: An incident is user impact plus an operational coordination problem. Google SRE describes clear command/operations/communications roles, working records and mitigation before full root-cause analysis.

blocks.md: An incident is user impact plus an operational coordination problem. Google SRE describes clear command/operations/communications roles, working records and mitigation before full root-cause analysis. Scope the blast radius, freeze unrelated changes, preserve evidence and communicate grounded impact/uncertainty. A suspected cause is not confirmed cause. Runbook actions need explicit owner authority/preconditions and expected effects; an incident is not permission to spend, deploy, delete data or expose secrets.

Own pure state is (epoch,phase) with phases running, paused, reconciling, ready. Legal path: pause running, inspect paused, approve reconciling, resume ready. Approve/resume require current snapshot, invariants_ok and NO unknown effects. Expected epoch must match; every accepted transition increments it. This is an immutable planner only: pause does not stop a process, resume does not start one, and caller booleans do not authenticate evidence. Actual atomic state publication and role authorization are not implemented.

blocks.title: Unknown acknowledgment must be reconciled before resuming
items: Begin (0,running). Pause yields (1,paused); inspect yields (2,reconciling). Consult authoritative inventory/idempotency records from the previous lesson,not only the failed caller acknowledgment.

A precommit failure can have rolled back; an after-commit failure may already have reserved inventory. If effects are still unknown, approve must fail. Record what source/revision/timestamp establishes the real state.
Only current reconciled evidence permits (3,ready), then a rechecked resume yields (4,running). A stale expected epoch 0 fails rather than applying an old operation to this new state.

blocks.caption: Expected (1,paused), (2,reconciling), (3,ready), (4,running); stale recovery epoch; unsafe or out-of-order recovery transition. Exact Python tuple output quotes phases. Complete pure source with strict evidence keys/bool types. It does not execute rollback, restart, external reconciliation, authorization, concurrent compare-and-swap or durable recovery.

blocks.md: Choose a stated hypothesis, failure point, allowed environment/blast radius, stop condition, owner, backup/restore and observation plan BEFORE injecting. Test precommit/postcommit lost acknowledgments, timeout, dependency failure, corrupt/missing artifacts and recovery replay on local/staging fixtures. Caught Python exceptions are not process kill, disk loss, power failure, network partition or multi-writer concurrency. Never inject failure into real user systems merely because a classroom simulation passed.

A runbook should name symptom/impact, scope/version, required access, current authoritative checks, exact bounded action, expected result/time, stop/escalation and rollback/restore verification. Include how to handle unknown outcomes and avoid duplicate effects. Backups need tested restore and recovery-point/time objectives, not only a green backup job. Recovery may preserve recent committed data differently from reverting a binary; do not equate rollback, replay and restore.

Verify reconciled business invariants, data freshness/pending effects, actual health/telemetry and user-critical flows, then restore traffic progressively under authority. ready is not automatic approval to operate: the toy flag assumes evidence supplied correctly. A pause may itself affect obligations or queued work; document and reconcile that impact. Do not erase corrupted/unknown evidence to make checks green. Preserve a timestamped action/owner/state log without credentials.

Separate mitigation, root cause, contributing conditions and corrective work. A blameless review describes observed timeline, impact, detection/response gaps, what worked, and owned verifiable follow-ups. Avoid inventing certainty or promising recurrence impossible. Exercise the updated runbook and verify the fix under the original failure hypothesis. Actual incident communications are representation and must follow the user's approved scope; this lesson sends none.

Independent transfer: enumerate phases/actions/evidence flags and prove approval/resume impossible with unknown effects or stale snapshots. Replay an old epoch after every transition and reject it. Map prior SQL pre/postcommit failpoints to distinct runbook investigations. Then list actual process/concurrency/restore tests still absent. A boolean state machine is a teaching precondition check, not an incident-management or disaster-recovery platform.

Sources: [Google SRE managing incidents](https://sre.google/sre-book/managing-incidents/), [incident response/mitigation](https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/), [Python SQLite recovery semantics context](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/sqlite3.html). Own phase machine and evidence flags are not the Google incident system or a real recovery procedure.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why is a ready phase not enough to resume real traffic?
guidedExercise.solution: Evidence flags may be stale/wrong, actual state publication/auth absent; need authoritative business/pending effects/data reconciliation, health/user-flow/restore checks, bounded operational authority and progressive traffic plan. Pure simulation and exceptions do not prove real process/storage/concurrency recovery.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Failure injection, recovery and runbooks" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Keep tested failure model explicit. (Test actual environment/failure modes separately.)
Authoritative state resolves uncertain acknowledgment. (Unknown effects block readiness.)
realWorldApplication: Used directly across production quantitative research, execution systems, and validation pipelines.
quantFinanceApplication: Applies rigorous engineering contracts to quantitative modeling and live trading infrastructure.
summary: Unknown committed effects and stale state must block this toy recovery gate.
Failure injection/runbooks need bounded authority, observations and actual restore/process tests; the pure phase planner performs no operational recovery.

options: No, the failure model is narrower
quiz.explanation: Keep tested failure model explicit. (Test actual environment/failure modes separately.)

quiz.prompt: Unknown committed effects remain. Can this planner approve?
quiz.explanation: Authoritative state resolves uncertain acknowledgment. (Unknown effects block readiness.)

quiz.prompt: Starting epoch 0, four accepted phase transitions end at what epoch?
What does expected_epoch guard against in this pure planner?
options: Atomic publication that prevents two concurrent writers from committing the same epoch
quiz.explanation: An optimistic version check has a narrow role. (Actual atomic concurrent publication is still absent.)

quiz.prompt: What makes a backup operationally meaningful?
quiz.explanation: Backup creation and recovery outcome differ. (Verify data/application consistency and timing.)
